subject: Logical Reasoning
introduction: Pattern recognition in SIMAK covers visual matrix puzzles (3×3 grids), analogy patterns (A:B :: C:?), and abstract figure series. The key is to identify WHAT changes and HOW it changes systematically across rows, columns, and diagonals. Common attributes: shape type, number of sides, rotation, shading, size, and count of elements.

key_formulas.name: Row rule
key_formulas.formula: \text{Check if each row follows the same pattern}

key_formulas.name: Column rule
key_formulas.formula: \text{Check if each column follows the same pattern}

key_formulas.name: Diagonal rule
key_formulas.formula: \text{Check if the diagonal has a consistent pattern}

key_formulas.name: XOR rule
key_formulas.formula: \text{R1 XOR R2 = R3 (shapes in 1 or 2 but not both appear in 3)}

tips_and_tricks: In 3×3 matrices: check ACROSS each row first — is there a consistent rule?
Then check DOWN each column — do columns follow the same rule?
Common rules: rotation (90°, 180°), mirror flip, adding element per step, alternating shading.
For analogies: DESCRIBE the A→B transformation in words, then apply same transformation to C.
XOR pattern: shapes in A and B appear in C only if they appear in EXACTLY ONE (not both) of A and B.
Count patterns: count elements in each cell — often increases by 1 along row or column.
For rotation: try 90° clockwise and counter-clockwise first.

worked_examples.title: Example 1: Matrix analogy — rotation
worked_examples.question: In a 3×3 matrix, row 1: upward arrow, right arrow, downward arrow. Row 2: left-shaded circle, fully-shaded circle, unshaded circle. Describe the pattern.
solution: Step 1: Row 1 — arrows rotate 90° clockwise: up→right→down.
Step 2: Row 2 — shading decreases: left-shaded→fully-shaded→unshaded... (or some consistent change).
Step 3: Identify the rule: each row shows a 90° rotation of the figure.
Step 4: Apply to Row 3 to find the missing cell.

worked_examples.title: Example 2: Figure analogy pattern
worked_examples.question: Square : Cube :: Circle : ?
solution: Step 1: A square is a 2D shape. A cube is the 3D version of a square.
Step 2: Similarly, what is the 3D version of a circle?
Step 4: The analogy rule: 2D shape : its 3D counterpart.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.explanation:
Rule: Item → Place where many such items are stored/displayed.
Books are found in a Library. Paintings are found in a **Museum** (or gallery). Museum is the most comprehensive storage/display place for paintings.
hints: What is a library for books? A place that stores/displays them.
Where are paintings collected and displayed?

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.explanation:
Rule: Professional → Place where they work.
Doctors work in hospitals. Teachers work in **schools** ✓
hints: Where does a doctor work? In a hospital.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.explanation:
Pattern: alternating triangles and circles, each increasing by one.
1△, 1○, 2△, 2○, 3△, 3○, **4△** ✓
hints: Alternating triangles and circles, count increases.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.explanation:
Rule: Word → Its opposite (antonym).
Hot↔Cold. Fast↔**Slow** ✓
hints: What is the opposite of Hot? Cold.
Apply the same rule: opposite of Fast?

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.explanation:
Rule: Tool → Its primary function.
Pen is used for writing. Knife is used for **cutting** ✓
hints: What is a pen used for? Writing.
Apply: what is a knife used for?

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question_text: Odd one out: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Tomato, Mango.
questions.explanation: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Mango are all sweet fruits. **Tomato** is botanically a fruit but is typically classified as a vegetable in culinary contexts — it's the odd one out in this grouping.
hints: What do Apple, Banana, Cherry, Mango have in common that Tomato doesn't?
All others are commonly eaten as sweet fruits.
Tomato is the odd one out.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question_text: Matrix (3×3). Each row: the number of sides of the shape increases by 1 across columns. Row 1: triangle, square, pentagon. Row 2: square, pentagon, hexagon. Row 3: pentagon, hexagon, ?
questions.explanation:
Row rule: each row starts with one more side than previous row. In each row, sides increase by 1 per column.
Row 3: Pentagon(5), Hexagon(6), **Heptagon(7)** ✓
hints: Each row: sides increase by 1 left to right.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.explanation:
Rule: Reverse the letter sequence.
ABCD reversed = DCBA.
LMNO reversed = **ONML** ✓

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question_text: Figure series: Each figure in the series has one more circle than the previous and one fewer square. Start: 1 circle, 4 squares. What is position 4?
questions.explanation:
Position 1: 1 circle, 4 squares.
Position 2: 2 circles, 3 squares.
Position 3: 3 circles, 2 squares.
Position 4: **4 circles, 1 square** ✓

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.explanation:
Rule: Creative work → who/what creates it.
Symphony is created by an Orchestra. Novel is created by an **Author** ✓
hints: Who creates a symphony? An orchestra.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question_text: Analogy: AZ BY CX DW — what comes next?
questions.explanation:
First letters: A,B,C,D → +1 → E.
Second letters: Z,Y,X,W → -1 → V.
Next: **EV** ✓

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question_text: Odd one out based on pattern: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, 63.
hints: The given value is 63 ≠ 65. So 63 is wrong.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question_text:
In a 3×3 number matrix:
Row 1: 1, 2, 3
Row 2: 4, 5, 6
Row 3: 7, 8, ?
What is the missing number?
questions.explanation:
The matrix fills with consecutive integers: 1-9.
Missing: position (3,3) = **9** ✓
hints: Numbers fill the matrix left to right, top to bottom.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question_text: Matrix rule: In each row, R1 XOR R2 = R3 (shapes appearing in EXACTLY ONE of the first two cells appear in the third). If cell (3,1) has: {circle, square} and cell (3,2) has: {circle, triangle}, what is cell (3,3)?
questions.explanation:
XOR: shapes in exactly ONE of the two cells go to the third.
Cell 1: {circle, square}. Cell 2: {circle, triangle}.
circle: in BOTH → excluded.
square: only in Cell 1 → included.
triangle: only in Cell 2 → included.

Cell 3: **{square, triangle}** ✓
hints: XOR = in exactly one but not both.
Circle is in both cells → excluded.
Square (only Cell 1) and Triangle (only Cell 2) → included. Answer: {square, triangle}.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.explanation:
Rule: FLOW reversed = WOLF. TRAP reversed = PART.
TRAP → PART ✓

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question_text:
Number matrix. Each cell = product of its row and column number:
Row 1: 1,2,3. Row 2: 2,4,6. Row 3: 3,6,?
Find the missing value.
hints: Each cell = row number × column number.

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question_text: In a figure series, each shape is rotated 90° clockwise AND one dot is added per step. Step 1: Right-arrow, 0 dots. Step 2: Down-arrow, 1 dot. Step 3: Left-arrow, 2 dots. Step 4: ?
questions.explanation:
Rotation: Right→Down→Left→**Up** (90° clockwise each step).
Dots: 0,1,2,**3** (add 1 each step).
Step 4: **Up-arrow, 3 dots** ✓

questions.subject: Logical Reasoning
questions.question_text: Letter-number analogy: B2 D4 F6 H8 ? J10

options.text: J10 is already given — what comes before? The blank is ? = J10

questions.explanation:
Pattern: B(2)=2, D(4)=4, F(6)=6, H(8)=8, J(10)=10.
Letters: every other letter (+2 each step).
Numbers: even numbers matching position (B=2nd letter→2, D=4th→4...).
The missing term between H8 and J10: I is 9th letter but the pattern skips odd letters. So the blank = **J10** which is already shown.

If the ? is the 9th term (after J10): L12 ✓
But if the pattern is B2,D4,F6,H8,J10 → ? = **L12**.
hints: Letters: B,D,F,H,J — every other letter (+2 each).
